items.original_title: Trump, Xi, Putin's Trilateral Evokes Images of Yalta and Beyond
items.rss_summary:
The trilateral meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin was billed as an opportunity for global cooperation — while raising fears that the leaders of the three largest nuclear powers are carving up spheres of influence. 
Even if the summit was light on concrete outcomes, the images of the leaders of the US, China and Russia at an unprecedented summit is likely to live on in history.
Elizabeth Economy, Stanford Professor and Hargrove Senior Fellow, discusses the trilateral meet

items.original_title: Aberdeen’s Galbraith on Ukraine and US-China Tensions
items.rss_summary: Lizzy Galbraith, Senior Political Economist at Aberdeen Investments, discusses the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit, with the leaders emphasizing stability while producing few immediate policy breakthroughs. Galbraith examines US-China tensions over technology and export controls, prospects for progress on the Russia-Ukraine war, and concerns that Ukraine and Europe could face renewed pressure to make concessions. She spoke with Guy Johnson on Bloomberg Brief. (Source: Bloomberg)
